subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Selected Surahs
overview: The short surahs at the end of the Qur’an, together with Surat Al-Fatiha, are recited every day in swalah and at home. In this sub-strand you will read and recite Al-Fatiha, An-Naas, Al-Falaq, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Masad, An-Nasr and Al-Kafirun, learn the basic meaning of each one, and practise the lessons they teach.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Fatiha: the opening of the Qur’an
objectives: Read and recite the seven verses of Surat Al-Fatiha correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of Surat Al-Fatiha.
State why Muslims recite Al-Fatiha in every swalah.
lessons.intro: Every rak’ah of swalah includes the same short surah. It praises Allah, asks for His help and begs for the straight path. That surah is Surat Al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Qur’an.
lessons.notes:
### The Opening of the Book
Surat Al-Fatiha is the first surah of the Qur’an. It is also called Ummul Qur’an, the Mother of the Qur’an, because it gathers praise of Allah and the dua a Muslim needs most. It has seven verses. The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that there is no swalah for the person who does not recite the Opening of the Book (Bukhari and Muslim). We therefore recite it in every rak’ah.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim — In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
2. Alhamdu lillahi Rabbil-alamin — All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.
3. Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim — The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
4. Maliki yawmid-din — Master of the Day of Judgement.
5. Iyyaka na’budu wa iyyaka nasta’in — You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
6. Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim — Guide us to the straight path.
7. Siratal-ladhina an’amta alayhim, ghayril-maghdubi alayhim wa lad-dallin — The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who have gone astray.

### Lessons for character
All praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of people, angels, jinn and every other creature. He is full of mercy, and He will judge on the Day of Judgement, so we prepare for that Day. A Muslim worships Allah alone and asks Allah alone for help. The straight path is the path of the prophets and the righteous. We ask to be kept away from those who knew the truth and turned against it, and from those who went astray.

Recite Al-Fatiha slowly in swalah and think of this meaning. Begin good work with Bismillah. When you need help, ask Allah first, then use the lawful means He has given you.

keyWords.meaning: the Opening; the first surah of the Qur’an, recited in every rak’ah of swalah
Mother of the Qur’an, another name for Surat Al-Fatiha
the straight path of guidance

examples.problem: A learner finishes a rak’ah of swalah but did not recite Al-Fatiha. What is missing, and why does it matter?
steps: Al-Fatiha is recited in every rak’ah.
The Prophet (S.A.W.) said there is no swalah for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.
The learner should learn the surah and recite it in the next prayer.
examples.answer: Surat Al-Fatiha is missing. It is required in every rak’ah, so the learner must recite it.

activity.title: Listen, then match the verses of Al-Fatiha
materials: A recording of Surat Al-Fatiha or a teacher reciting it
Flash cards: one set with the seven verses in transliteration, one set with the English meanings
steps: Listen quietly to a correct recitation of Surat Al-Fatiha from your teacher or a digital device.
Recite after the teacher, verse by verse, then recite the whole surah on your own.
In pairs, match each verse card with its meaning card.
Write the seven meanings in your notebook and tell your partner why Al-Fatiha is recited in every swalah.

practice.question: How many verses does Surat Al-Fatiha have, and where is it placed in the Qur’an?
practice.answer: It has seven verses and it is the first surah of the Qur’an.

practice.question: Give the meaning of ‘Iyyaka na’budu wa iyyaka nasta’in’.
practice.answer: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.

practice.question: Why do Muslims recite Surat Al-Fatiha in every swalah?
practice.answer: It is required in every rak’ah. The Prophet (S.A.W.) said there is no swalah for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book. It also praises Allah and asks for guidance.

practice.question: What does a Muslim ask for in the last two verses of Al-Fatiha?
practice.answer: Guidance to the straight path, the path of those Allah has favoured, not the path of those who earned anger or went astray.

summary: Surat Al-Fatiha has seven verses and opens the Qur’an.
It praises Allah, declares that we worship and ask only Him, and begs for the straight path.
It is recited in every rak’ah of swalah.

lessons.title: Surat An-Naas: seeking refuge with the Lord of people
objectives: Recite Surat An-Naas correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of its six verses.
Describe the whisper a Muslim seeks protection from.
lessons.intro: Just before you sleep, a quiet worry or a sudden wish to do wrong can pass through the mind. Surat An-Naas teaches the believer to ask Allah, the Lord of people, for protection from that whisper.
lessons.notes:
### A surah of protection
Surat An-Naas is the last surah of the Qur’an. It has six verses. Together with Surat Al-Falaq it is one of the Mu’awwidhatayn, the two surahs of seeking refuge. The Prophet (S.A.W.) recited An-Naas, Al-Falaq and Al-Ikhlas before he slept (Bukhari).

### The verses and their meaning
1. Qul a’udhu bi Rabbin-nas — Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.
2. Malikin-nas — The King of mankind.
3. Ilahin-nas — The God of mankind.
4. Min sharril-waswasil-khannas — From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws.
5. Alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas — Who whispers into the hearts of mankind.
6. Minal-jinnati wan-nas — From among the jinn and mankind.

### What the whisper is
Waswas is an evil suggestion that pushes a person towards a sin and then pulls back. It can come from the jinn, especially Shaytan, or from people, such as a friend who says, “Nobody will see you.” Allah is named three times in this surah: He is the Lord who cares for people, the King who controls them, and the only God they worship. Protection is sought from Him alone.

When you feel pushed to lie, take what is not yours, or answer a parent rudely, stop. Say “A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim” and recite Surat An-Naas. Choose a friend who reminds you of Allah instead of a friend who whispers wrong.

keyWords.meaning: Mankind; the last surah of the Qur’an
an evil whisper that urges a person to do wrong and then withdraws
the two surahs of seeking refuge, Al-Falaq and An-Naas

examples.problem: During a test, a classmate whispers, “Look at my paper. The teacher is not watching.” Which surah answers this moment, and what should the learner do?
steps: The whisper urges cheating and then hopes to disappear.
Surat An-Naas seeks refuge from whispers that come from people as well as from jinn.
The learner refuses, recites An-Naas quietly if there is time, and does his or her own work.
examples.answer: Surat An-Naas. The learner should refuse to cheat and seek refuge with Allah from that whisper.

activity.title: Match the verses of An-Naas with their meanings
materials: Flash cards of the six verses
Flash cards of the six meanings
steps: Listen to Surat An-Naas recited by the teacher or from a digital device.
Repeat each verse until you can recite the surah smoothly.
In groups, sort the verse cards and match each one with its meaning.
Write the meaning in your notebook and give one example of a whisper a Grade 4 learner should refuse.

practice.question: What three names of Allah are used in the first three verses of Surat An-Naas?
practice.answer: Lord of mankind, King of mankind and God of mankind.

practice.question: Who can the evil whisper come from, according to the last verse?
practice.answer: From among the jinn and from among mankind.

practice.question: What should a Muslim do when a whisper urges him or her to sin?
practice.answer: Stop, seek refuge with Allah, recite Surat An-Naas, and refuse the sin.

summary: Surat An-Naas asks Allah for protection from evil whispers.
Those whispers can come from jinn or from people.
Muslims recite it, together with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq, before sleeping.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Falaq: refuge from harm in creation
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Falaq correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of its five verses.
Name the harms from which the surah seeks protection.
lessons.intro: Night can feel unsafe, and some people wish others harm because of envy. Surat Al-Falaq teaches a Muslim to place every fear in the care of Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.
lessons.notes:
### Lord of the daybreak
Surat Al-Falaq has five verses. Falaq means the daybreak, the moment Allah splits the darkness and brings the morning. The surah orders the believer to seek refuge in the Lord of that daybreak. It is the partner of Surat An-Naas, and the Prophet (S.A.W.) used both when he sought protection.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Qul a’udhu bi Rabbil-falaq — Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.
2. Min sharri ma khalaq — From the evil of what He created.
3. Wa min sharri ghasiqin idha waqab — And from the evil of darkness when it settles.
4. Wa min sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad — And from the evil of those who blow on knots.
5. Wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad — And from the evil of an envier when he envies.

### Four kinds of harm
First, some created things can harm, such as a dangerous animal, a disease or a person’s evil choice. Second, darkness can hide danger. Third, “those who blow on knots” refers to people who try to harm others by magic. Fourth, envy is the wish that a blessing be taken away from someone else. A Muslim asks Allah for protection from all four, and a Muslim must never be the cause of them.

Recite Al-Falaq in the morning, in the evening and before sleep. Do not envy a classmate’s marks, clothes or friends. Make dua for them instead. Never try to harm anyone by magic or by any other secret means. Trust that Allah brings light after every darkness.

keyWords.meaning: the daybreak; the surah that seeks refuge in the Lord of the daybreak
envy; wishing that another person’s blessing be removed
ask Allah to protect you from harm

examples.problem: A girl is upset because her friend received a new uniform and she did not. She hopes the uniform gets torn. Which part of Al-Falaq corrects her, and what should she do instead?
steps: Hoping that a blessing is destroyed is envy.
The last verse seeks refuge from the envier when he envies.
She should recite Al-Falaq, thank Allah for what she has, and be happy for her friend.
examples.answer: The verse about the envier. She should leave the envy, make dua for her friend and ask Allah to protect her heart.

activity.title: Listen to the translation of Al-Falaq
materials: Digital device with a recorded recitation and translation, or the teacher reading both
steps: Listen to Surat Al-Falaq, then listen to a recorded or read translation.
In groups, list the four harms named in the surah.
Discuss one way a learner can avoid envy at school.
Write the list and the decision in your notebook, then recite the surah together.

practice.question: What does the word falaq mean in this surah?
practice.answer: The daybreak.

practice.question: Name the four evils from which Surat Al-Falaq seeks protection.
practice.answer: The evil of what Allah created, the evil of darkness when it settles, the evil of those who blow on knots, and the evil of the envier when he envies.

practice.question: When did the Prophet (S.A.W.) recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas together?
practice.answer: Before he slept.

summary: Al-Falaq seeks refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.
It asks protection from created harm, darkness, magic and envy.
A Muslim recites it for protection and refuses to envy or harm others.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Ikhlas: Allah is One
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Ikhlas correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of its four verses.
State how the surah shapes belief in Allah.
lessons.intro: If someone asks, “What do Muslims believe about Allah?” a short surah of four verses can answer. Surat Al-Ikhlas is pure belief: Allah is One, and nothing is like Him.
lessons.notes:
### A surah of pure belief
Surat Al-Ikhlas has four verses. Ikhlas means sincerity. The surah sincerely describes Allah without adding any partner, parent or child. The Prophet (S.A.W.) said that it is equal to one third of the Qur’an (Bukhari). Muslims recite it often in sunnah prayers and, with Al-Falaq and An-Naas, before sleep.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Qul huwallahu Ahad — Say: He is Allah, the One.
2. Allahus-Samad — Allah, the Eternal, whom all creatures need and who needs no one.
3. Lam yalid wa lam yulad — He neither begets nor is He begotten.
4. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad — And there is none comparable to Him.

### Lessons for belief and character
Allah is One in His Lordship and in worship. He was not born, and He has no children. He does not need food, sleep, helpers or a family. Every person, including the strongest king, needs Allah. Nothing in creation equals Him, so no person, star, idol or idea may be worshipped beside Him.

A Muslim shows this belief by praying only to Allah, swearing only by Allah, and refusing to treat a creature as if it shared Allah’s power. When you do a good deed, do it for Allah, not for show. That is ikhlas in daily life. Learn these four short verses until you can recite them without looking, and teach the meaning to a younger child at home.

keyWords.meaning: sincerity; the surah that declares Allah is One
the One; Allah has no partner
the Eternal whom everyone needs and who needs no one

examples.problem: A boy says, “Allah has a son, like people do.” Which verse of Al-Ikhlas answers him?
steps: The third verse says Allah neither begets nor is begotten.
The fourth verse says nothing is comparable to Him.
The boy should be corrected gently with the meaning of the surah.
examples.answer: Lam yalid wa lam yulad: He neither begets nor is He begotten. Nothing is like Allah.

activity.title: Sort the four verses of Al-Ikhlas
steps: Listen to Surat Al-Ikhlas from the teacher or a digital device.
Recite it three times as a group.
Match each verse with its meaning without looking at the board.
Write one sentence that begins, “Because Allah is One, I will…” and share it with the group.

practice.question: Give the meaning of ‘Qul huwallahu Ahad’.
practice.answer: Say: He is Allah, the One.

practice.question: What does As-Samad tell us about Allah?
practice.answer: Allah is the Eternal. All creatures need Him, and He needs no one.

practice.question: What did the Prophet (S.A.W.) say about the reward of Surat Al-Ikhlas?
practice.answer: It is equal to one third of the Qur’an.

practice.question: State one way a learner shows ikhlas at school.
practice.answer: He or she does good deeds for Allah, not for show, and worships Allah alone.

summary: Al-Ikhlas says that Allah is One and that nothing is like Him.
Allah has no children and no parents, and He needs no one.
The surah is equal to one third of the Qur’an and is recited often.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Masad: wealth cannot replace faith
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Masad correctly.
Explain its basic meaning in simple words.
Apply its lesson about wealth and opposing the truth.
lessons.intro: Being a relative of a good person does not make someone good, and having money does not make someone safe. Surat Al-Masad tells of a man who was close to the Prophet (S.A.W.) in family, yet opposed his message.
lessons.notes:
### The surah and who it names
Surat Al-Masad, also called Surat Al-Lahab, has five verses. It speaks about Abu Lahab, an uncle of the Prophet (S.A.W.), and about Abu Lahab’s wife. They opposed the Prophet and worked against his message. The surah warns that their wealth and effort will not save them.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Tabbat yada Abi Lahabiw wa tabb — May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
2. Ma aghna anhu maluhu wa ma kasab — His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained.
3. Sayasla naran dhata lahab — He will burn in a fire of blazing flame.
4. Wamra’atuhu hammalatal-hatab — And his wife, the carrier of firewood.
5. Fi jidiha hablun min masad — Around her neck is a rope of twisted fibre.

His wife is called the carrier of firewood because she carried thorns and placed them where they would harm the Prophet (S.A.W.). The surah shows that she shared in the wrong.

### Lessons to live by
Family ties do not replace iman. Abu Lahab was an uncle of the Prophet, yet he rejected the message. Money, status and hard work in a bad cause cannot protect a person on the Day of Judgement. Helping to harm the truth is itself a serious wrong.

Use any money you are given in a halal way: buy what you need, share with a classmate who has less, and do not show off. If relatives or friends dislike your salah, remain polite and still obey Allah. Do not join anyone in hurting a person because of his or her faith.

keyWords.meaning: twisted fibre; the surah also called Al-Lahab
an uncle of the Prophet (S.A.W.) who opposed Islam
to be of use or to save someone

examples.problem: A rich man refuses to pray and says his money will protect him. What does Surat Al-Masad say about that idea?
steps: The second verse says Abu Lahab’s wealth and what he gained will not benefit him.
Wealth cannot take the place of faith and obedience.
A Muslim thanks Allah for money and spends it in obedience.
examples.answer: Wealth will not save a person who rejects faith. Money cannot replace obedience to Allah.

activity.title: Discuss the lesson of Al-Masad
materials: Flash cards of the five verses and their meanings
steps: Listen to the teacher recite Surat Al-Masad, then listen to the translation.
In groups, match each verse with its meaning.
Discuss two lessons: wealth cannot replace faith, and we must not harm the cause of truth.
Write the lessons in your notebook in your own words.

practice.question: Who was Abu Lahab?
practice.answer: An uncle of the Prophet (S.A.W.) who opposed Islam.

practice.question: What is the meaning of ‘His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained’?
practice.answer: His money and the things he earned will not save him.

practice.question: Give one way a learner can apply Surat Al-Masad when he or she is given money.
practice.answer: Use it in a halal way, share with someone in need, and do not think that money replaces salah or good character.

summary: Al-Masad warns about Abu Lahab and his wife, who opposed the Prophet (S.A.W.).
Wealth cannot save a person who rejects faith.
A Muslim does not use money or effort to harm the truth.

lessons.title: Surat An-Nasr: victory, praise and forgiveness
objectives: Recite Surat An-Nasr correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of its three verses.
Show how a Muslim behaves after success.
lessons.intro: Winning a race or doing well in class can make a person boast. Surat An-Nasr teaches the opposite. When help and victory come, a Muslim praises Allah and asks Him for forgiveness.
lessons.notes:
### A short surah about a great victory
Surat An-Nasr has three verses. Nasr means help, and fath means victory or conquest. The surah speaks of the time when Allah’s help came and people entered Islam in large numbers. Muslims understand this victory as the conquest of Makkah, when the city opened to the Prophet (S.A.W.) and many people accepted Islam.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Idha ja’a nasrullahi wal-fath — When the help of Allah comes and the victory.
2. Wa ra’aytan-nasa yadkhuluna fi dinillahi afwaja — And you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds.
3. Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirh, innahu kana tawwaba — Then glorify the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.

### Lessons for daily life
Success comes from Allah. People may work hard, but the help that brings a good result is from Him. After success, the believer does not insult those who lost. The believer says Subhanallah and Alhamdulillah, and asks Allah to forgive any mistake made along the way. Allah loves to accept repentance. He is At-Tawwab, the One who accepts those who turn back to Him.

When you pass a test, win a match or finish memorising a surah, thank Allah in front of your friends without boasting. If you were rude while competing, apologise and ask Allah to forgive you. Help a classmate who has not yet succeeded.

keyWords.meaning: help; the surah about Allah’s help and victory
victory or conquest
the One who accepts repentance

examples.problem: Two teams finish a class quiz. The winning team laughs at the others. How does Surat An-Nasr guide the winners?
steps: Victory is a help from Allah.
The surah commands praise and asking forgiveness, not pride.
The winners should thank Allah and treat the other team kindly.
examples.answer: They should praise Allah, avoid mocking, ask forgiveness if they were unkind, and respect the other team.

activity.title: Meaning of An-Nasr in groups
steps: Listen to a recitation of Surat An-Nasr from the teacher or a digital device.
Listen to the translation and match each of the three verses to its meaning.
In groups, discuss what a Muslim says and does after a success at school.
Write three points in your notebook and recite the surah together.

practice.question: What do the words nasr and fath mean?
practice.answer: Nasr means help, and fath means victory or conquest.

practice.question: What does the third verse tell the believer to do when victory comes?
practice.answer: Glorify and praise the Lord, and ask His forgiveness.

practice.question: Which victory do Muslims understand this surah to refer to?
practice.answer: The conquest of Makkah, when many people entered Islam.

summary: An-Nasr has three verses about Allah’s help and victory.
After success, a Muslim praises Allah and asks forgiveness.
Allah is At-Tawwab, always ready to accept repentance.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kafirun: worship belongs to Allah alone
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Kafirun correctly.
Explain the basic meaning of its six verses.
Show how a Muslim stays firm and still treats others fairly.
lessons.intro: Learners live, learn and play with neighbours of different faiths. Surat Al-Kafirun draws a clear line in worship: a Muslim does not worship what others worship, and does not force others in religion.
lessons.notes:
### A clear surah
Surat Al-Kafirun has six verses. It was revealed when the Prophet (S.A.W.) was asked to mix his worship with the worship of the idols of Makkah, taking turns from year to year. The surah refuses that mixture completely.

### The verses and their meaning
1. Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun — Say: O disbelievers.
2. La a’budu ma ta’budun — I do not worship what you worship.
3. Wa la antum abiduna ma a’bud — Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
4. Wa la ana abidun ma abadtum — Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship.
5. Wa la antum abiduna ma a’bud — Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship.
6. Lakum dinukum wa liya din — For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.

### Firm faith and fair treatment
The surah is repeated so that the refusal is complete: not now, and not later. A Muslim’s worship is for Allah alone. “For you is your religion, and for me is my religion” means each person is responsible for his or her own faith. It agrees with the words of the Qur’an that there is no compulsion in religion (Qur’an 2:256). It does not mean a Muslim may join another form of worship for a day and return later.

Be polite to classmates and neighbours. Share the playground fairly and never insult their faith. At the same time, do not bow to idols, join prayers that are not to Allah, or hide your salah because someone laughs. When it is time to pray, pray. Your religion is a trust from Allah.

keyWords.meaning: the disbelievers; the surah that separates Islamic worship from other worship
religion or way of life
nobody is forced to accept a religion

examples.problem: Friends invite a Muslim learner to bow in front of a picture as part of their worship, and they say he can pray his own prayer tomorrow. What does Al-Kafirun teach him to answer?
steps: The surah says: I do not worship what you worship.
It also says this will not change later.
He can refuse gently and remain a good friend in ordinary play.
examples.answer: He does not join that worship, now or later. He stays kind, and he keeps his own salah for Allah alone.

activity.title: Flash cards for Al-Kafirun
steps: Listen to Surat Al-Kafirun recited clearly by the teacher or from a digital device.
Recite after the recording until the group can say all six verses.
Sort the cards and match every verse with its meaning.
Discuss, then write, one way to be polite to people of another faith and one way to keep your own worship pure.

practice.question: Give the meaning of the last verse of Surat Al-Kafirun.
practice.answer: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.

practice.question: Why is the refusal to mix worship repeated in the surah?
practice.answer: To show that a Muslim will not worship other than Allah, neither now nor later.

practice.question: Does ‘to you your religion’ allow a Muslim to miss salah in order to please friends? Explain.
practice.answer: No. It means faith is not forced on others. A Muslim still keeps his or her own worship of Allah.

summary: Al-Kafirun refuses any mixing of worship.
A Muslim worships Allah alone, now and in the future.
People are not forced in religion, and a Muslim still remains firm.

lessons.title: Living by the seven selected surahs
objectives: Link each selected surah to one daily action.
Choose surahs to recite before sleep and inside swalah.
Explain why holding to these teachings is a way of valuing the Qur’an.
lessons.intro: Reading a surah is the first step. The surah has done its work when a learner tells the truth, leaves envy, praises Allah after success and prays on time. This lesson gathers the seven surahs into daily habits.
lessons.notes:
### Where the seven surahs belong in the day
Surat Al-Fatiha is recited in every rak’ah of swalah. Surat Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas are the three surahs the Prophet (S.A.W.) recited before sleeping. Al-Falaq and An-Naas are also recited in the morning and the evening for protection. Al-Kafirun keeps worship pure. An-Nasr guides the heart after any success. Al-Masad warns against trusting money more than Allah.

### One teaching from each surah
- Al-Fatiha: praise Allah, ask only Him for help, and stay on the straight path.
- An-Naas: refuse the whisper to sin, whether it comes from a person or from Shaytan.
- Al-Falaq: ask Allah for protection and do not envy anyone.
- Al-Ikhlas: worship Allah alone and do good for Him, not for show.
- Al-Masad: do not think wealth can replace faith, and do not help in harming the truth.
- An-Nasr: when you succeed, say Alhamdulillah and ask forgiveness instead of boasting.
- Al-Kafirun: be fair to people of other faiths, and do not mix your worship with theirs.

### Appreciating the surahs
A learner appreciates these surahs by reciting them correctly, learning the meaning, and obeying what they teach. Skipping salah, cheating because a friend whispered it, or mocking another team after a win, goes against the same surahs the tongue has recited. Each night, recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas, blow lightly into the hands and wipe the face and body, as the Prophet (S.A.W.) did. Each day, let one verse change one action.

keyWords.meaning: to put a teaching into a real action
to value something by respecting it and following it

examples.problem: Before bed, Hassan recites only songs from the radio and then finds it hard to wake for Fajr. He also hid a classmate’s pen because he envied the classmate’s marks. Which surahs correct these two habits?
steps: Before sleep he should recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas.
Envy is the harm named at the end of Al-Falaq.
Fajr still requires Al-Fatiha in every rak’ah.
examples.answer: He should recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas before sleep, leave envy as Al-Falaq teaches, and pray Fajr with Al-Fatiha.

activity.title: Sort teachings under the seven surah names
materials: Cards with daily actions and short meanings
steps: Listen again to a short recitation of any two selected surahs from a digital device.
In groups, place each action card under the surah that teaches it. For example, place ‘do not boast after winning’ under An-Nasr.
Check one another’s sorting and correct any card that is under the wrong surah.
Each learner writes seven lines in the notebook: the name of a surah and one action he or she will do this week.

practice.question: Which three surahs did the Prophet (S.A.W.) recite before sleeping?
practice.answer: Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas.

practice.question: Match the action to the surah: refusing to cheat after a friend whispers. Which surah fits best?
practice.answer: Surat An-Naas.

practice.question: Give one action that shows you appreciate Surat Al-Fatiha.
practice.answer: Recite it in every rak’ah of swalah and ask Allah for the straight path, then follow that path by obeying Him.

practice.question: What should a Muslim say and do after winning a game, according to An-Nasr?
practice.answer: Praise Allah, ask His forgiveness for any mistake, and avoid mocking the losers.

summary: Al-Fatiha belongs in every rak’ah, and Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas are recited before sleep.
Each selected surah corrects a real habit, such as envy, pride, showing off or mixing worship.
Valuing the surahs means reciting them and living by them.

quiz.question: Why is Surat Al-Fatiha recited in every swalah?
options: It is required in every rak’ah
It is recited only on Friday
quiz.explanation: The Prophet (S.A.W.) said there is no swalah for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of ‘Alhamdu lillahi Rabbil-alamin’?
options: Guide us to the straight path
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds
Say: He is Allah, the One
quiz.explanation: This is the second verse of Surat Al-Fatiha.

quiz.question: Which surahs are the Mu’awwidhatayn, the two surahs of seeking refuge?
quiz.explanation: Al-Falaq and An-Naas both begin by seeking refuge with Allah.

quiz.question: According to Surat An-Naas, the evil whisper can come from whom?
quiz.explanation: The last verse says ‘from among the jinn and mankind’.

quiz.question: Which harm is named in the last verse of Surat Al-Falaq?
quiz.explanation: The verse asks refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies.

quiz.question: What does Surat Al-Ikhlas say about Allah having children?
quiz.answer: He neither begets nor is He begotten. Allah has no children.
quiz.explanation: The third verse, Lam yalid wa lam yulad, gives this meaning.

quiz.question: What lesson does Surat Al-Masad teach about wealth?
options: Wealth cannot save a person who rejects faith
quiz.explanation: Abu Lahab’s wealth and what he gained would not avail him.

quiz.question: After a victory, what does Surat An-Nasr tell the believer to do?
options: Glorify Allah and ask His forgiveness
quiz.explanation: The last verse says to glorify the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness.

quiz.question: A friend says, ‘Worship my idol today and Allah tomorrow.’ Which surah answers this?
quiz.explanation: Al-Kafirun says the believer does not worship what they worship, now or later.

quiz.question: Which three surahs did the Prophet (S.A.W.) recite before going to sleep?
quiz.explanation: This is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Fatiha is recited in swalah.

quiz.question: Which action shows that a learner values these surahs?
options: Reciting them for show and then cheating
Learning the meaning and obeying it
quiz.explanation: Appreciating the surahs means reciting them and adhering to their teachings.

sources: KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 1.0 Qur’an, Sub-strand 1.1 Selected Surahs
Qur’an: Surat Al-Fatiha, An-Naas, Al-Falaq, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Masad, An-Nasr and Al-Kafirun; Qur’an 2:256
Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: recitation of Al-Fatiha in swalah; recitation of Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Naas before sleep; virtue of Al-Ikhlas
